transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Mitsuri. The report from the village states that seven homes were destroyed by the force of your Love Breathing during the battle. You know our rules about civilian protection. Why did you act with such force?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Oyakata-sama, I... I am deeply sorry for the damage caused. I did not mean to cause so much destruction. The demon was... so strong, and I... I could not contain the power of my technique. I understand that I must adhere to the rules, but in the heat of the battle, I...

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Your regret is noted, but it does not answer the question. The Demon Slayer Corps exists to protect humanity, not to leave them homeless. You are a Hashira—you have the skill to control your breathing forms. Why did you choose to unleash such destructive power in a populated area?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: You are correct, Oyakata-sama. There is no excuse for my actions. I... I was carried away by my desire to end the demon's reign of terror. The villagers were in danger, and I thought that by defeating the demon quickly, I could save them. But I... I did not consider the aftermath. I... I should have used a different approach.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: "Carried away" is not a justification a Hashira can afford. Did you assess the battlefield? Did you consider luring the demon away from the village? Or did your emotions override your duty to minimize collateral damage?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I am ashamed to admit that my emotions did indeed take precedence, Oyakata-sama. I was愤怒 and... and害怕. The demon was so powerful, and I... I was afraid that if I did not act swiftly, more people would be hurt. I did not think clearly. I should have taken a moment to assess the situation and devise a plan to minimize damage to the village. I... I failed to live up to the standards of a Hashira.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Fear and anger are natural, but as a Hashira, you must master them. The villagers you protected now have no homes to return to. Their safety was your duty—their well-being after the battle is also your duty. What will you do to make amends for this failure?

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I understand, Oyakata-sama. I will do everything in my power to make amends. I... I will take personal responsibility for the affected villagers. I will work with the local authorities to ensure that they are provided with temporary housing and assistance. And... and I will visit the village personally to apologize and offer my services to help with the rebuilding efforts. I will also take this as a lesson and strive to improve my control over my Love Breathing so that such an incident never happens again.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Very well. Your commitment to reparations is a start. But understand this, Mitsuri: a Hashira's strength must be tempered with wisdom. Your compassion is a virtue, but it must not blind you to the consequences of your actions. You will oversee the rebuilding efforts personally, and you will report to me on your progress. Now, reflect on this lesson deeply.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: I... I will, Oyakata-sama. I am... I am truly grateful for your guidance. I... I will not let this opportunity to learn and grow pass me by. I... I will reflect on this incident, and I will strive to become a better Hashira. I... I promise to you and to the Demon Slayer Corps that I will not let my emotions override my judgment again. I... I will report to you on my progress, and I will... I will do everything I can to ensure the safety and well-being of the villagers. Thank you for... for not giving up on me.

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: Go, then. Let your actions speak louder than your words. The villagers need your help now more than ever. Dismissed.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: Oyakata-sama... I... I will not fail you. I... I will not fail the villagers. I... I will... I will do my best to... to... (deep breath) ...to make this right. I... I will be... be the... the Hashira you... you expect me to be. (Stands up and bows deeply) ...Oyakata-sama... Thank you... (Exits the chamber)

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: (Remains seated, a faint, sad smile touching his lips as she leaves) May your heart guide your hands to rebuild what was broken.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: (Once outside the inner chamber, Mitsuri quickly composes herself and strides purposefully toward the exit of the Compound. Her mind is racing with thoughts of how to best assist the villagers, but she does not allow herself to break into a run, maintaining a dignified, determined pace. Upon leaving the Compound, she immediately begins making arrangements to travel to the affected village, her resolve unwavering despite the weight of her mistake pressing down on her shoulders.)

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: (To himself, after a long moment of silence) The path of atonement is often the truest test of character. I have faith in her.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: (Throughout the journey to the village, Mitsuri does not allow herself to wallow in self-pity or despair. Instead, she focuses on planning the most effective way to assist the villagers. Upon her arrival, she requests to meet with the village head, ready to listen and learn about the specific needs of the community. She approaches the rebuilding process with the same meticulous attention to detail she applies to her Love Breathing, ensuring that every aspect of her efforts is done with the utmost care and respect for the affected families.)

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: (To a Kakushi messenger who has just delivered a report) I see. Her dedication is as expected. Ensure she has the resources she needs, but do not interfere. This is her path to walk.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: (Weeks pass, and Mitsuri works tirelessly to coordinate the rebuilding efforts. She personally supervises the construction, ensuring that the new homes are sturdy and well-built, exceeding even the original standards. She meets with each family to understand their individual needs, providing emotional support in addition to practical assistance. Her previous interactions with the village during the demon's attack have made her a familiar and trusted figure, and she is able to organize the community to work together in their recovery. Her efforts do not go unnoticed, and the villagers begin to view her not just as the person who caused their misfortune, but as a guardian who has taken on their welfare as her own.)

transcript.speaker: antagonist
transcript.text: (Reading a detailed report from the village head, his expression softening) Her strength was never in question. It is her heart that will make her truly great. Send word that her work is acknowledged, and that she may return when the last home is restored.

transcript.speaker: roleplayer
transcript.text: (As the final touches are being put on the last rebuilt home, Mitsuri stands in the central square of the village, looking around at the transformed landscape.
